title: Natural boundary isomorphisms for the integral compact-support scalar mate
statement: Fix a prime l and a finite-field datum D with l ≠ D.p. Let X,Y be finite-type schemes over D.k, f : X → Y a separated finite-type relative morphism, and c a compactification of f. Assume NativeGeometry l and fix a coefficient construction P, its StageAction at c, source and target realizations, and an index E of finite coefficient subfields of PadicAlgCl l [def-sf-locally-finite-adic-compact-support-data, def-sf-locally-finite-adic-realization-data, def-sf-constructible-exceptional-coefficient-construction-data, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Write L_T for the raw integral-to-rational localization on T, Q_T for inclusion of E in the common-stage pair category, Sec_T for derived sections, P_c for compact support with completed integral coefficients, P_n for native compact support, and C_T for derived extension along the integral map of the realization on T [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data]. There exist natural isomorphisms b : L_X ⋙ (Q_X ⋙ stage.system.functor ⋙ target.J) ⋙ Sec_Y ≅ integralInclusion_X ⋙ P_c ⋙ C_Y and d : integralInclusion_X ⋙ C_X ⋙ P_n ≅ L_X ⋙ (Q_X ⋙ source.J ⋙ actual) ⋙ Sec_Y. For every finite-Tor integral input K [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], b.hom at its integral inclusion is a composite of three arrows: the recorded rationalLeft arrow after Q_Y, target.J and Sec_Y; target.integral at the integral compact-support value of K; and C_Y applied to inverse sfQcqsCompactSupportRealization at K. The component of d is a composite of two arrows: P_n applied to inverse source.integral at K, and inverse operationTransport at source.J(Q_X(rationalization(K))). The rational arrow is an actual arrow in the raw rational category, with heterogeneous equality to the prescribed rationalLeft component; all five arrows have the displayed heterogeneous component equalities. No scalar mate or lifted native natural transformation is asserted.

proof.text: The rational finite compact-support functor is the scalar extension of the integral linear Hom map. On integral arrows, baseChange sends one tensor f to one tensor F(f). Hence localization commutes with this action by a natural isomorphism with identity components.

proof.text: Compose the stage inclusion comparison, whose components are identities, with the recorded equality of the finite action and rationalLeft. Whisker by target.J and derived sections. Follow by the target integral realization and derived extension of inverse sfQcqsCompactSupportRealization. This constructs a natural source boundary isomorphism b.

source.place: Definition 6.7.6, Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; original finite-comparison steps 4 and 8

proof.text: Evaluate the two boundary isomorphisms on a finite-Tor integral input. The proved finite-stage comparison supplies a raw rational arrow r, its heterogeneous equality to rationalLeft and its map formula. The integral-action localization comparison has identity components; its image under the target realization is an identity. Expand the boundary components, use this identity and the functor identity law, and obtain the first three and last two prescribed arrows separately. The rationalization input aliases are definitionally equal, so their component comparison is a reflexive heterogeneous equality. There is no scalar mate or lift in this argument.

theorem native_integral_scalar_boundaries [G : NativeGeometry.{u} l]
    (source : Realization l X) (target : Realization l Y)
    (stage : StageAction l D hl P c) (E : Index l (PadicAlgCl l)) :
    ∃ (b :
    sfRationalConstructibleLocalization l (Coefficient l (PadicAlgCl l) E) X ⋙
        (GeneralAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.inclusion
          (l := l) (Ω := PadicAlgCl l) (Y := X) E ⋙ stage.system.functor ⋙ target.J) ⋙
        (sections l Y).mapDerivedCategory ≅
      (sfIntegralConstructible l (Coefficient l (PadicAlgCl l) E) X).ι ⋙
        PurCompactSupport.image (PurCompactSupport.completed l
          (Coefficient l (PadicAlgCl l) E)) c ⋙
        pbcDerivedExtend ((target.coefficient E).integralMap l Y))
      (d :
    (sfIntegralConstructible l (Coefficient l (PadicAlgCl l) E) X).ι ⋙
        pbcDerivedExtend ((source.coefficient E).integralMap l X) ⋙
        PurCompactSupport.image (nativeCoefficients l) c ≅
      sfRationalConstructibleLocalization l (Coefficient l (PadicAlgCl l) E) X ⋙
        (GeneralAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.inclusion
          (l := l) (Ω := PadicAlgCl l) (Y := X) E ⋙ source.J ⋙ actual l c) ⋙
        (sections l Y).mapDerivedCategory),
      ∀ K : finiteTorConstructibleIntegralCategory l
          (Coefficient l (PadicAlgCl l) E) X,
    let rationalInput :=
      (rationalization l (ULift.{u} (PadicAlgCl l)) (finiteField l E) X).obj K
    let input := (GeneralAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.inclusion
        (l := l) (Ω := PadicAlgCl l) (Y := X) E).obj rationalInput
    ∃ (A B : sfRationalConstructibleCategory l
          (Coefficient l (PadicAlgCl l) E) Y) (r : A ⟶ B),
      HEq r ((P.ring.rationalLeft c (finiteField l E)).hom.app rationalInput) ∧
    ∃ (M₁ M₂ M₅ : DerivedCategory
          (proEtaleRingModules Y (ringSheaf l Y)))
      (a₀ : (sections l Y).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        ((sfRationalConstructibleLocalization l
          (Coefficient l (PadicAlgCl l) E) X ⋙
          (GeneralAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.inclusion
          (l := l) (Ω := PadicAlgCl l) (Y := X) E ⋙ stage.system.functor ⋙ target.J)).obj
            ((PurCompactSupport.finiteTorIntegralInclusion l
              (Coefficient l (PadicAlgCl l) E) X).obj K)) ⟶ M₁)
      (a₁ : M₁ ⟶ M₂)
      (a₂ : M₂ ⟶ (PurCompactSupport.image (PurCompactSupport.completed l
          (Coefficient l (PadicAlgCl l) E)) c ⋙
          pbcDerivedExtend ((target.coefficient E).integralMap l Y)).obj K.obj)
      (a₄ : (pbcDerivedExtend ((source.coefficient E).integralMap l X) ⋙
          PurCompactSupport.image (nativeCoefficients l) c).obj K.obj ⟶ M₅)
      (a₅ : M₅ ⟶ (sections l Y).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        ((sfRationalConstructibleLocalization l
          (Coefficient l (PadicAlgCl l) E) X ⋙
          (GeneralAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.inclusion
          (l := l) (Ω := PadicAlgCl l) (Y := X) E ⋙ source.J ⋙ actual l c)).obj
            ((PurCompactSupport.finiteTorIntegralInclusion l
              (Coefficient l (PadicAlgCl l) E) X).obj K))),
      HEq a₀ ((sections l Y).mapDerivedCategory.map
        (target.J.map ((GeneralAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.inclusion
          (l := l) (Ω := PadicAlgCl l) (Y := Y) E).map r))) ∧
      HEq a₁ ((target.integral E).hom.app
          ((sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l D.k
            (PurCompactSupport.coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) c
            (Coefficient l (PadicAlgCl l) E)).obj
              ((PurCompactSupport.finiteTorIntegralInclusion l
                (Coefficient l (PadicAlgCl l) E) X).obj K))) ∧
      HEq a₂ ((pbcDerivedExtend ((target.coefficient E).integralMap l Y)).map
          ((sfQcqsCompactSupportRealization l (Coefficient l (PadicAlgCl l) E)
            D.k (PurCompactSupport.coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) c).inv.app
              ((PurCompactSupport.finiteTorIntegralInclusion l
                (Coefficient l (PadicAlgCl l) E) X).obj K))) ∧
      HEq a₄ ((PurCompactSupport.image (nativeCoefficients l) c).map
          ((source.integral E).inv.app
            ((PurCompactSupport.finiteTorIntegralInclusion l
              (Coefficient l (PadicAlgCl l) E) X).obj K))) ∧
      HEq a₅ ((operationTransport l c).inv.app (source.J.obj input)) ∧
      b.hom.app ((PurCompactSupport.finiteTorIntegralInclusion l
          (Coefficient l (PadicAlgCl l) E) X).obj K) = a₀ ≫ a₁ ≫ a₂ ∧
      d.hom.app ((PurCompactSupport.finiteTorIntegralInclusion l
          (Coefficient l (PadicAlgCl l) E) X).obj K) = a₄ ≫ a₅
